title: Cherry Blossom Road
description:
April on the Han River cherry blossom road. The flowers were white.
Daeun stopped under the canopy and looked up.
"Minjun, it's like it's snowing." Every gust brought petals down, and she laughed.
An afternoon with no uniform, no register. One petal settled on her shoulder.

description_if_known.cherry_grey_view:
April on the Han River cherry blossom road.
Daeun stopped under the canopy and looked up. "Minjun, it's like it's snowing."
{name} looked up too. It was the first time the cherry blossoms looked grey.
Even {name} knew it wasn't the flowers that had changed.
"...Minjun? Are you okay?" Daeun peered at his face. One petal settled on her shoulder.

choices.text: Brush the petal from her shoulder.
choices.result_text:
When his fingertips touched her shoulder, Daeun smiled a little. "...That tickles."
She caught the petal in her palm. "This year's blossoms — I saw them with you, Minjun."
He wanted to hold onto that sentence for a long time.

choices.text: Say nothing — watch the petals fall together.
choices.result_text:
Neither of them spoke. Falling petals make no sound, but it felt like he could hear them.
"...I've never had a moment like this," Daeun said quietly.
Neither had {name}.

choices.text: "Let's see them together next year too."
choices.result_text:
Daeun's eyes went round, and then she smiled without hiding it.
"...That's a promise now. I remember all of these, you know."
Cherry blossoms last a week. The promise stayed.

title: Cherry Blossom Road
description:
"I even checked the bloom map. This is the peak." Jiyeon led the way.
April on the Han River cherry blossom road. The flowers were white.
She'd picked the route with data, but once under the canopy her steps slowed.
"...Better than I expected." The wind brought petals down, and one landed in her hair.

description_if_known.cherry_grey_view:
"I even checked the bloom map. This is the peak." Jiyeon led the way.
April on the Han River cherry blossom road. {name} looked up.
It was the first time the cherry blossoms looked grey. He knew it wasn't the flowers that had changed.
"Oppa." Jiyeon turned around. "...What's going on in your head these days." Her voice wasn't joking.
A petal landed in her hair.

choices.text: Pick the petal out of her hair.
choices.result_text:
"...What do you think you're doing." She said it without moving away.
The composure that slipped for half a second came right back. "...If there's another one, get that too."
There wasn't. He pretended there was.

choices.text: Say nothing — watch the petals fall together.
choices.result_text:
Jiyeon was quiet for a long while.
"...If I were at the office right now, I'd be in my second meeting."
By now {name} knew that was her way of saying it was beautiful.

choices.text: "Let's see them together next year too."
choices.result_text:
"You talk like a project proposal." Jiyeon laughed. "...Approved. Next April, same spot."
She actually put it in her phone calendar.

title: The Sea, After Five Years
description:
First train to the east coast. Daeun sat by the window, watching for the direction the sea would appear. She never once dozed off.

At a shop by the station they picked out swimsuits. Daeun flipped the price tag over twice and reached for the cheapest one — and when {name} held out a prettier one, her hand stopped. She hesitated, and her face went red.
"Something like this... it's been so long. I don't know if it'll suit me." She said it that way, and still turned once before the fitting-room mirror.

On the sand, the salt wind tossed her hair. The moment the first wave reached her feet, Daeun laughed out loud — a laugh bigger than {name} had ever heard from her, childlike, forgetting even to cover her mouth.
"Minjun, it's been... five years since I saw the sea."
At the end of the words, for a second, her throat caught. On the list of things Seoul had quietly taken from her was the sea — and this was the face of getting it back after five years.

choices.text: "Next year we're staying overnight."
choices.result_text:
Daeun answered loud enough to beat the waves.
"Okay. ...Promises like that scare me — but if it's you making it, I'm not scared."

On the train back, Daeun fell asleep against the window. A few shells she'd picked up were wrapped in a handkerchief on her lap, and even half-asleep her hand didn't let them go.
As the sea drew away outside the glass, {name} watched her sleeping face for a long time. A day that gave back five years was riding home to Seoul in a handful of palm-sized shells.

choices.text: Say nothing — take her hand and run to the waterline.
choices.result_text:
When {name} took her hand and ran for the water, Daeun grabbed his arm, half scream, half laugh. The instant the cold reached her ankles —
"It's cold! It's c—" and still she didn't step back. "...But I don't want to get out. Just a little longer."

Wet sand held their feet, and each time a wave rushed in and pulled back, the two of them swayed a little. Every time, Daeun gripped {name}'s arm tighter.
Beside someone laughing off five years all at once, {name} just laughed along too — not even noticing his cuffs soaking through with saltwater.

title: Haeundae
description:
"Haeundae is my turf." From the moment they stepped off at Busan Station, an accent crept into Jiyeon's speech — the hometown tongue she kept pressed down in Seoul.
The market alleys, the best mulhoe place, haggling over the parasol — she really was on home ground, not a hitch in the words she traded with the vendors.

But when he suggested going in the water, Jiyeon didn't move from under the parasol. She hugged her knees and just stared at the sea.
"...Oppa." The sunglasses stayed on. {name} couldn't tell where the eyes behind them were looking.
"Don't laugh." A beat later, her voice dropped a little.
"I... can't swim."
The one who'd called it her turf had the face of someone who'd never once been into that sea.

choices.text: Laugh — try not to, and fail.
choices.result_text:
Watching {name} try not to laugh and fail, "Hey!" — Jiyeon flung a fistful of sand. Her sunglasses slipped a little, and through the gap her eyes shot him a glare. The composure broke for exactly half a second.
"...Growing up in Haeundae doesn't mean everyone can swim." The recovery was quick, as always. She pushed the sunglasses back up, as if nothing had happened.

That day Jiyeon went in only ankle-deep. No further. But in that shallow water, every time a wave came she'd secretly catch {name}'s sleeve — and {name} pretended not to notice.

choices.text: "Then I'll hold on to you. Just to the knees."
choices.result_text:
Jiyeon looked at {name} for a long moment over her sunglasses. A weighing kind of silence. Then she took them off. For the first time, her eyes were simply there, bare.
"...To the knees. Cross it and you're dead." And the hand she held out trembled a beat ahead of the waves.

Each time the water touched her knees, that hand tightened. {name} had never seen the proud one grip anything so hard. Not laughing, holding that hand to the end — that was {name}'s only job that day.
On the way back, Jiyeon tossed it out: "...Maybe chest-deep next time." Knowing she wouldn't, and saying it anyway — that was the kind of person she was.

title: Fireworks, a Profile
description:
Yeouido. The riverside was packed with crowds out for the fireworks festival.
At the meeting spot, {name} didn't recognize Daeun at first. The one always in a convenience-store uniform or plain clothes was, tonight, in a dress he'd never seen. Her hair done differently, light makeup, strands lifting in the river wind.

"...First time seeing me out of uniform, right?" she said first — not sure where to put her eyes, hands going to the hem of her dress, but not hiding either.
Three seconds of silence while {name} chose his answer. Those three seconds stretched strangely long.

choices.text: "You look beautiful." — before the three seconds run out.
choices.result_text:
"You look beautiful." Before the three seconds ran out, {name} said it.
Daeun tried to hold back a smile and failed. Covering her flushed face with the back of her hand,
"...Even if it's a lie, tonight I'll believe it."
It wasn't a lie. Right then the first firework went off — boom, over the river. Everyone looked up at once, and the light poured down in colors over Daeun's dress, over her laughing face. {name} had no wish to take the words back.

choices.text: When the fireworks burst, watch her profile instead of the sky.
choices.result_text:
Boom — every time the sky lit, color landed on Daeun's face and vanished. Red, green, gold.
Daeun watched the fireworks; {name} watched the one watching them.
"...Minjun, aren't you going to look?" she asked, feeling his gaze.
"I'm looking." An answer given while they watched two different things. A beat later Daeun caught what he meant, and — face turned to the sky — went red to the tips of her ears. And still, not hiding it, she smiled a little.

choices.text: Take her hand before the crowd can push between you.
choices.result_text:
Just before the crowd surged, {name} took Daeun's hand. She startled, looked at him, then squeezed back. Small, but unmistakable.
"If we lose each other, we'll never find our way back," Daeun said, loud enough not to drown in the crowd.
The words carried far past the crowd of that night. As fireworks burst overhead one after another, neither of them let go. Even their palms sweating together was no reason to.

title: Off Duty
description:
The Yeouido fireworks festival. Someone waved from the crowd — Jiyeon, in a hoodie and sneakers, barely any makeup.
No suit, no heels, no business cards. Hard to believe it was the same 'Han Jiyeon' {name} knew.
"If anyone from the office saw me, they'd faint." She pulled the hood lower and smirked. Not minding others' eyes — the face, tonight, of someone let loose from them.
When the crowd surged toward the river, Jiyeon took {name}'s hand first. Playing it casual, and yet unmistakable.

choices.text: Re-grip her hand — fingers interlaced.
choices.result_text:
When {name} re-gripped her hand with fingers interlaced, Jiyeon glanced down at it. Half a second.
"...It's because of the crowd." The recovery was quick, as always. And still she didn't pull away — if anything, her fingers tightened between his.
The first firework burst over the river. While Jiyeon looked up at the sky, {name} felt only the warmth of that hand. Whatever went off up there, the one certain thing right now was this hand held in his.

choices.text: "I like this version of you better."
choices.result_text:
"I like this version of you better." When {name} said it, Jiyeon stopped walking.
"...Which part." Even in the dark, the red creeping up the tips of her ears under the hood was visible.
"Never mind. Watch the fireworks." A snap — and then she pulled the hood off. The hood she'd kept pulled down, gone at that one line.
Her hair lifted in the river wind, and above it the first firework broke. {name} watched, a long while, the light settling over her uncovered face.

choices.text: When the fireworks burst, watch her profile instead of the sky.
choices.result_text:
Boom — the light repainted Jiyeon's face in shifting colors. Red to gold, then to blue.
Catching {name}'s gaze, she turned. "...What are you looking at."
"The fireworks." "Liar." She smirked — this time without the thorn.
More than the fireworks bursting in the sky, it felt like something quieter had gone off much closer. Jiyeon pretended to watch the sky again, but the held hand stayed exactly as it was.

title: First Snow, That Convenience Store
description:
The first snow came on the way home. Daeun was waiting in front of the convenience store — the one where everything started.
Two cans of coffee in her hands.
"First snow calls for these." She held one out. "Remember us standing here, just like this?"
The snow was visible only in the light of the sign, then vanished into the dark.

description_if_known.daeun_sea_5years:
The first snow came on the way home. Daeun was waiting in front of the convenience store — the one where everything started. Two cans of coffee in her hands.
At the summer sea she said she hadn't seen in five years, he had watched the seasons come back to her one by one. This time it was first snow.
"First snow calls for these." She held one out. "Remember us standing here, just like this?"
The snow was visible only in the light of the sign, then vanished into the dark.

choices.text: "I remember. It was this same coffee."
choices.result_text:
"Right. You looked so... cold back then, Minjun." Daeun laughed, then let the sentence trail off.
"Not anymore. Now you look like someone who's with someone."
Until the cans went cold, neither of them suggested going inside.

choices.text: Say nothing — tap the cans together, like a toast.
choices.result_text:
Clink. The sound of can on can rang small in the snowing alley.
"...What are we toasting to?" "First snow."
Daeun smiled. "Then we'll have to do this every year."

title: The Wipers
description:
The first snow started inside the car on the drive home. The wipers pushed it away twice.
The alley in front of his place. Even with the car stopped, Jiyeon didn't tell him to get out. Then she turned the wipers off.
Snow began to pile on the windshield. The lights smeared away until only the inside of the car was left.
"Oppa, wait," she said. "Let's stay like this."

description_if_known.jiyeon_cant_swim:
The first snow started inside the car on the drive home. The wipers pushed it away twice.
The alley in front of his place. Even with the car stopped, Jiyeon didn't tell him to get out. Then she turned the wipers off.
Snow began to pile on the windshield.
The woman who was afraid of the water was watching the snow pile up to the very end. The same one who never went past the shallows at Haeundae.
"Oppa, wait," she said. "Let's stay like this."

choices.text: Turn off the engine — listen to the snow settling.
choices.result_text:
When the engine died, the world went quiet. Snow makes no sound, but he could almost hear it landing.
"...I'm not the kind of person who does this," Jiyeon said, watching the windshield.
"I know." "...I'm only like this in front of you."
Until the glass was covered white, neither of them got out.

choices.text: "Want to walk a little, before it melts?"
choices.result_text:
Jiyeon looked at {name}. "...Walking in the first snow? Oppa, you're such an old soul."
She was already unbuckling her seatbelt as she said it.
Under the alley streetlight, two sets of footprints went into the snow first.
